title: He Scored 776 Runs at a Strike Rate of 237. India Has Called Up a 15-Year-Old.
excerpt: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who shattered Chris Gayle's sixes record and won the IPL Orange Cap, will break Sachin Tendulkar's age record when he debuts for India in Ireland.
body:
When the Board of Control for Cricket in India announced its squads for the upcoming tours of Ireland and England on June 6, one name stood apart from all the rest. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, a 15-year-old left-handed opener from Bihar who had just finished the most extraordinary Indian Premier League season anyone had ever seen at any age, was named in all three white-ball assignments — the Ireland T20Is, the England T20Is, and the squad for the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya later this year.

If he takes the field in Belfast on June 26 as expected, he will become the youngest male cricketer to represent India in senior international cricket, surpassing the record set by Sachin Tendulkar, who was 16 years and 205 days old when he debuted against Pakistan in Karachi in November 1989.

## An IPL Season That Rewrote the Record Books

Sooryavanshi's IPL 2026 campaign for the Rajasthan Royals defied every convention of what a teenager is supposed to be capable of against the best bowlers in the world. He scored 776 runs in 16 matches at a staggering strike rate of 237.31 — the highest in a single IPL season by any batter who has scored more than 500 runs. He hit 72 sixes across the tournament, shattering Chris Gayle's long-standing record for the most maximums in a single IPL campaign.

His century against Sunrisers Hyderabad — 103 off 37 balls, the third-fastest hundred in IPL history — came in an Eliminator. His three consecutive scores of 90-plus in the playoffs left hardened international captains searching for adjectives.

"I think he's my new favourite player," Australia captain Pat Cummins said after his Sunrisers Hyderabad side was dismantled by the teenager. "He hits the ball so hard. You've got to be right on the money as a bowler, because if you're not, it's going a long way."

Kumar Sangakkara, who coached Sooryavanshi at the Royals, was unequivocal. "With everything Vaibhav has shown against some of the best bowlers in the world, I think he's more than ready to take on any challenge that you throw at him," Sangakkara said. "I'm sure that he'll get that call-up very, very soon."

## A Career That Has Always Run Ahead of Schedule

Sooryavanshi's trajectory has never followed conventional timelines. He earned his maiden Ranji Trophy cap at 12. At 13, he became the youngest player ever signed in an IPL auction when the Rajasthan Royals picked him up for INR 1.10 crore at the 2025 mega auction. In the Under-19 format, he cracked a 58-ball century against Australia — the fastest Youth Test hundred by an Indian.

This season, however, was the one that made the conversation about age irrelevant. Trevor Penney, the Royals' assistant coach, put it simply: "I've never seen a 15-year-old bat like that. Even if he was 25, I think we'd be talking about him."

## The Weight of Comparison

The inevitable comparisons to Tendulkar have been embraced rather than deflected. Former India opener Kris Srikkanth urged the selectors to fast-track Sooryavanshi months ago, drawing a direct line to how Tendulkar himself was inducted at a young age. "Sachin also played at such a young age," Srikkanth said. "The same thing can be done for this boy in white-ball cricket."

Dale Steyn, one of the greatest fast bowlers of all time, went further. "He's going to be bigger than Sachin Tendulkar and Virat Kohli put together at the end of his career," Steyn said, before adding a note of caution. "I would caution how you manage him and look after him, because with great responsibility comes great reward. But there's a big threat there that you could lose him at some point if you don't look after him well enough."

Graeme Swann, the former England off-spinner, was at the ground in Chandigarh for one of Sooryavanshi's playoff innings. "It was the most audacious knock from a 15-year-old kid," Swann said. "He's at that age where he's completely fearless because he's not had failure."

## What It Means for the Diaspora

For the estimated four million Indian-origin residents in the United Kingdom, the timing of Sooryavanshi's likely debut could not be more poignant. The Ireland T20Is begin on June 26 in Belfast, and the five-match England series that follows — in Chester-le-Street, Manchester, Nottingham, Bristol, and Southampton — will bring him to cities with some of the largest British-Indian populations in the country.

The last time Indian cricket produced a teenage prodigy of this magnitude, millions of NRIs followed Tendulkar's career from living rooms in London, Toronto, and New Jersey. Sooryavanshi's story is beginning in the same way — except this time, the diaspora will be able to watch his earliest steps in person.

Shreyas Iyer, newly appointed as India's T20I captain after replacing Suryakumar Yadav, will lead the squad. Jasprit Bumrah has been rested for the white-ball series but remains in the Asian Games squad, where India will chase gold in Aichi-Nagoya in September.
